transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Okonkwo, thank you for coming back to see me. I need to talk to you about the paperwork we gave you when you left the hospital.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am here. My family is worried. The clinic said they cannot help me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry. I made a mistake. I gave you a clinic for your follow-up that does not take your insurance. That was my fault.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I went all that way. I told my children I was fine and had a plan. Now I look like a man who cannot even follow a simple paper.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is not just the paper. In my community, we must be strong. My people look to me. If I cannot manage my own health, how can I lead?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's look at the insurance details. The clinic I picked is a private center. Your insurance only works with certain hospitals. I did not check the list before I wrote it down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I have no doctor now. I have no one to check the medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you know what it is to have people asking why you are failing? My daughter is very upset.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to get this sorted for you quickly. Here is what we are going to do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know why this happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, I chose the wrong clinic. I should have checked your insurance first. I am truly sorry for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is a big problem for me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I have already called Dr. Anya at the City Health Clinic. She is in your insurance network.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Dr. Anya? I do not know her.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: She is a specialist in your care. I have already sent her your files. I spoke with her ten minutes ago.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When can I see her?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Tomorrow morning at ten. I have the appointment booked for you right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have to tell my family I must go again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will give you a letter. It will say the hospital made a mistake and we are fixing it. You can show this to your family so they know it was not your fault.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A letter?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. I will write that I gave you the wrong information and that the hospital is responsible. This way your reputation is protected.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That would be better.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am also going to call the office manager here. We are changing how we print the discharge papers so the computer checks the insurance automatically. This will stop this from happening to other people.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope so.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Here is the address for Dr. Anya. It is on this paper. Do you see the map at the bottom?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I see it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Your job is just to arrive at ten tomorrow. I will call you at nine to make sure you have a ride. Is that okay?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. That is okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry again for the stress I caused you and your children. I will see you in the hallway in five minutes with that letter.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to express distress without interrupting and uses no rushing language throughout the encounter.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked once regarding the map/address.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry'), takes full personal responsibility ('That was my fault'), and maintains this under pushback.

R.justification: Resident engages emotional bids by offering a letter to protect the patient's reputation and references the stress caused to the children, though specific emotions are not named back as often as generic validation.

T.justification: Plan includes specific next steps (Dr. Anya), a timeline (tomorrow at 10), the patient's role (arrive at 10), and a systemic prevention strategy (automatic insurance checks).
